item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J01995","case1_error":"Equates the two-patient remainder with the remainder after only one patient, then doubles an already combined total.","case2_error":"Uses twice the entire actual toddler count instead of adding eight duplicate counts and subtracting three missed toddlers.","reason":"The first confuses which patients a remainder includes and double-counts that subtotal; the second applies duplicate-count multiplicity to the whole population.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01996","case1_error":"Provides unsupported conflicting numbers after the correct difference formula, ultimately claiming $15 instead of $11.","case2_error":"Incorrectly evaluates the final addition of $11.53 change to the correct $68.47 subtotal as $130.72 instead of $80.","reason":"The first supplies unsupported numbers without locating an arithmetic failure; the second locates the error in the final addition step.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01997","case1_error":"Inserts an unsupported $3,000 tax expense; the stated profit tax does not justify that amount.","case2_error":"Sets feeding costs equal to purchase costs, omitting the stated 20% increase.","reason":"The first invents an unexplained expense value; the second explicitly uses an incorrect cost relation that drops the percentage increase.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01998","case1_error":"Uses incorrect expense and leftover relations, ignores the stated $18 remainder, and reports salary minus necessities as taxes.","case2_error":"Appends an unsupported $280 total to the correct earnings formula, which gives $221.","reason":"The first constructs incorrect financial relations; the second gives a wrong final number after a correct formula.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01999","case1_error":"Subtracts only Ryan's quarter-share, omitting Chris's withdrawal.","case2_error":"Multiplies the combined bedroom time by three again and divides work among four people instead of three.","reason":"The first omits one required withdrawal; the second misrepresents an equality and the number of workers, independently of bathroom wording.","judgment":"different"}]}
